why: Replay and Field are a coordinate system, not a memory type — which means many kinds of memory can share one substrate instead of each getting its own architecture. But typing is only useful if it changes the rules: a procedural memory must not be reinforced by the same evidence rule as a factual one, and an encountered claim must not become established knowledge just because it was recorded. So a record carries a type and a scope, Ch'en validates a delta against its type, and consolidation has gates.

coordinates.law: M = (R, F, tau, sigma): replay reference, field reference, memory type, and scope/permissions
coordinates.rule: type and scope determine how a record is interpreted and accessed; they do not change where it lives

typed_validation.law: every Micronaut may propose a LearningDelta, and Ch'en validates it according to the memory type it targets
typed_validation.rule_mismatch: a delta whose substrate does not match its type's learning rule is refused rather than reinterpreted
examples: a semantic record is reinforced by corroboration and contradiction, not by execution success
a procedural record is reinforced by execution outcomes
a research record is reinforced by verified yield and retrieval efficiency
an ingress record is reinforced by parsing fidelity

consolidation.law: not every observation becomes a permanent semantic fact

gates.working_to_episodic: provenance plus a phase trace: an episode records what happened
gates.episodic_to_consolidated: verified corroboration above the declared threshold, and the type's own rule satisfied

consolidation.example: a claim encountered on a website may be preserved as an episode ('this was encountered') while semantic knowledge waits for verification

views.law: each Micronaut may hold a specialized memory view over the same substrate
views.rule: a view filters what it reads by type; it never widens scope and never bypasses the read check

invariants.MT1: memory is addressed by (R, F, tau, sigma): the substrate is unchanged by typing and a type is an interpretation, not a separate store
invariants.MT2: the fifteen types are declared with what each preserves and its replay/field dimensions
invariants.MT3: every type names a learning rule, and Ch'en validates a delta against its target type
invariants.MT4: a delta whose substrate does not match its type's rule is refused as a mismatch rather than reinterpreted
invariants.MT5: consolidation is gated: observation to working needs provenance, working to episodic needs provenance and a phase trace, and episodic to consolidated needs verified corroboration above the threshold
invariants.MT6: an encountered claim is preserved as an episode without becoming established knowledge, and only verification moves it
invariants.MT7: a Micronaut's memory view filters by type and never widens scope or bypasses the read check
invariants.MT8: the same fold serves every memory type: no memory type introduces a second phase cycle
invariants.MT9: promotion is deterministic and reports the gate that refused it
invariants.MT10: typing does not launder provenance: a consolidated record still names the episodes it was consolidated from
